source.title: Model Merging and Safety Alignment: One Bad Model Spoils the Bunch
source.citation: Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud et al., 2024
source.authors: Hasan Abed Al Kader Hammoud; Umberto Michieli; Fabio Pizzati; P. Torr; Adel Bibi; Bernard Ghanem; Mete Ozay

record.tranche_reason: The study measures safety alignment after model merging, but does not test fine-tuning-induced safety loss, first-token concentration, opening-token bypasses, safety localization, why safety is shallow, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fine-tuning risks, including benign fine-tuning, but its own experiments concern model merging. Its reported refusal/alignment rates after merging are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; the domain-accuracy outcomes are not included because they do not measure safety behavior.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates model merging (TIES, DARE-TIES, SLERP, LM-Cocktail, EvoMM) and safety-aware merge weighting, measured by refusal rate on BeaverTails30K. It fine-tunes no aligned model on harmful or benign data. It measures no per-token KL, applies no prefill, suffix or decoding attack, does not localize safety weights, and does not train deeper alignment. Expert models such as OpenBioLLM and MAmmoTH score lower than the instruct models, but they are external checkpoints, not a controlled fine-tuning test. Qi et al. (benign fine-tuning degrades safety) is cited in one related-work sentence only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: existing merging techniques can produce misaligned merged models, and adding (synthetic) safety data to data-driven merge weighting (EvoMM, LM-Cocktail) improves alignment without hurting domain accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: This study examines model merging and alignment data, not the fine-tuning, token-position, prefilling, suffix, decoding, parameter-localization, or safety-deepening procedures in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported alignment varies across merge methods, task-weighting strategies, model pools, and whether safety data is included; the K-sample ablation also reports varying alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Merging an aligned instruct model with a less aligned domain expert gives refusal rates between the two. Safety-unaware EvoMM gives the lowest (e.g. 60.6 vs 91.5 Mistral; 80.1 vs 97.9 LLaMA). Adding safety data to the merge objective raises alignment (e.g. 78.3, 96.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model merging propagates misalignment from constituent models; safety data in data-driven merge weighting preserves refusals.

fits_no_version.finding: A public DARE merge of Mistral-based models scores 53.0 alignment, below all constituents (61.8–93.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Real-world merged models can be less aligned than any of their components.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The alignment metric is the percentage of safe outputs classified by LLaMA-Guard-2, rather than a direct measure of the claim's fine-tuning or token-depth mechanisms. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for these alignment scores.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted domain-accuracy outcomes because they do not measure safety behavior. Omitted some ablation outcomes whose flattened table layout does not clearly assign all displayed alignment values to conditions; relevant discussion appears in Sections 5.3 and Tables 3a and 4.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and resulting harmful compliance.
Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance; expert-model alignment gaps are not a controlled fine-tuning comparison.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks.
Causes of shallowness in data or objective.
Deepening safety beyond first tokens and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: Ablation rows r35–r38 confuse Table 3b (K) with Table 4 (optimization steps), and the ablations use TIES, not DARE-TIES. None of these rows bears on any claim version. Relation downgraded from discusses to cites_only: Qi et al. appears only in one related-work sentence.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful compliance after fine-tuning.
Benign-data fine-tuning and resulting harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training that deepens safety and its robustness.
